html:
The Battle of Bosworth Field was fought on 22 August 1485 near Market Bosworth in Leicestershire, in the middle of England. Henry Tudor beat and killed King Richard III and became King Henry VII.

It was the last big battle of the Wars of the Roses, a long fight for the crown of England between the houses of Lancaster and York. Richard, of York, had taken the throne in 1483 in place of his young nephews, who vanished in the Tower of London. Henry, an exile with a thin Lancastrian claim, landed in Wales with about 2,000 soldiers paid for by France. Richard met him with a larger army. But the powerful Stanley family stood to one side and would not commit. When Richard saw Henry riding apart with a small guard, he charged straight at him. At that moment the Stanleys came in on Henry's side. Richard was cut down, the last English king to die in battle.

Henry married Elizabeth of York, joining the two houses, and founded the Tudor dynasty, which ruled until 1603. His son was Henry VIII and his granddaughter Elizabeth I. Richard's bones were found in Leicester in 2012.
